sections.h2: Where is Greenville, SC, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Greenville is the county seat of Greenville County, in the Upstate region of South Carolina at the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. It sits roughly halfway between Atlanta, about 145 miles southwest, and Charlotte, about 100 miles northeast. The Reedy River runs through the center of the city.

The 2020 census counted 70,720 residents, which made Greenville the sixth largest city in the state, and the metro area holds close to one million people. The city grew 21.1 percent between 2010 and 2020.

sections.h2: How did Greenville grow from a village to a regional city?
sections.html:
The land was Cherokee hunting ground until the 1777 Treaty of Dewitt's Corner ceded it to South Carolina. Greenville County was created in 1786, and Lemuel J. Alston founded the village of Pleasantburg in 1797. The name changed to Greenville in 1821, the village was incorporated in 1831, and it became a city in 1869.

Furman University moved here in 1851. By 1915 Greenville was known as the Textile Center of the South, with as many as 18 or 19 mills. Michelin moved its North American headquarters to the area in 1984, and BMW opened its first plant outside Germany nearby in 1994. The Liberty Bridge at Falls Park opened in 2004.

Greenville's economy was built on textiles and now leans on advanced manufacturing and automotive production. Employers and headquarters named in the city's entry include Michelin, Prisma Health, Bon Secours, Duke Energy, Synnex, United Community Bank, ScanSource and Sage Automotive Interiors.

The former Donaldson Air Force Base, now the South Carolina Technology and Aviation Center, hosts Lockheed Martin's F-16 production line, 3M and an electric vehicle test track. The city is also a freight hub for FedEx Express.

The mix of manufacturing, healthcare, banking and logistics means Greenville does not depend on a single employer. When a Greenville house is slow to sell, the cause is usually specific to the house, such as condition, title, tenants or timing.

sections.h2: Which areas and neighborhoods make up Greenville?
sections.html:
Greenville has a defined downtown and several distinct areas around it. The city's entry names the Village of West Greenville, the West End, Cleveland Park and the Southernside community. The city itself describes a wide variety of neighborhoods supported by active neighborhood associations.

Downtown features include:

  • Falls Park on the Reedy, with the Liberty Bridge and waterfalls
  • The Peace Center for the Performing Arts
  • The Greenville County Museum of Art
  • Bon Secours Wellness Arena, a 16,000-seat venue
  • Fluor Field at the West End, home of the Greenville Drive

The 22-mile Swamp Rabbit Trail runs through the city, and 4.5 miles were added in 2023.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools work in Greenville?
sections.html:
Interstate 85 runs along the southeast edge of the city, with spur routes I-185 and I-385 connecting to downtown. US 123, US 25, US 29 and US 276 also serve the city. Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport, in Greer, is the state's third busiest airport, with more than 2.56 million passengers in 2023. Greenville Downtown Airport is the state's busiest general aviation airport.

Greenlink runs the local bus system, and Amtrak's Crescent serves the train station.

The Greenville County School District covers all of the city. It is the largest district in South Carolina, with 19 high schools, 24 middle schools and 52 elementary schools. Colleges inside city limits include Bob Jones University and Greenville Technical College, and Furman University is in the wider area. Ask the district office for the school zone of a given address.

sections.h2: What does Greenville weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Greenville has four distinct seasons and a humid subtropical climate. The average January daily temperature is 42.2 degrees and July averages 79.9 degrees. Annual precipitation runs about 47 to 50 inches, and average snowfall is about 4 inches, mainly from January through March.

The record high is 107 degrees on July 1, 2012, and the record low is minus 6 on January 30, 1966. The average growing season is 217 days. Have heating and cooling service records ready, and walk the yard after a heavy rain to see where water collects.

sections.h2: How do Greenville County property taxes and a sale interact?
sections.html:
Greenville County sends real estate tax bills in late October, and payment is due January 15 with no penalty. After January 15 the Tax Collector adds 3 percent, after February 1 it adds 10 percent, and after March 16 it adds 15 percent. The office is at 301 University Ridge, Suite S-1100, and it is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at 864-467-7050.

January 15Due with no penalty; last day for 4 percent legal residence application

The county uses January 1 as its date of record, so if a house changes hands after that date, both the prior owner's and the new owner's names can appear on that year's bill.

The 4 percent legal residence assessment applies to owner-occupied homes and includes a credit that exempts the school operation tax. The county says a seller who has already moved out would likely not qualify.

A sale also matters to the next owner. The county says a sale can be an assessable transfer of interest that revalues the property at a current market value, with an effective appraisal date of December 31 of the sale year, and the 15 percent cap no longer applies to those transfers. Notices for increased values after a transfer typically carry a 90-day appeal period.

Delinquent properties go to a county tax sale at the Greenville Convention Center, 1 Exposition Drive, and bidders must register at least 30 days ahead.

sections.h2: What are the closing steps and costs in Greenville County?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded at the Greenville County Register of Deeds, 301 University Ridge, Suite S-2100. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and it asks recorders to arrive before 4:30. The main line is 864-467-7240. The office says it cannot assist in preparing deeds or other documents, so those must be finished before recording.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for the first $500 of value plus $1.30 for each additional $500, per the Department of Revenue. By that formula a $300,000 sale works out to roughly $780. The Register of Deeds also links a transfer tax calculator and exemption list on its recording page.

A South Carolina attorney handles the closing, since the state Supreme Court treats deed preparation, title work and closing supervision as the practice of law. The seller also provides a written property condition disclosure before contract signing, unless the sale is exempt. Estate fiduciary sales and transfers between spouses are among the exemptions in the state code.

sections.h2: What city rules should Greenville sellers check?
sections.html:
The City of Greenville regulates short-term rentals according to a property's zoning classification, after more residents began offering homes on sites such as Airbnb and VRBO. The page we read does not list the permit steps or zones, so a buyer who plans to rent should ask the city's Planning and Development office before relying on a rental plan.

Ask the city, too, about open permits and any code complaints on the property. Cleaning those up before a sale keeps a closing from stalling over paperwork.

faqs.q: When are Greenville County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15, with no penalty if paid by then. The county adds 3 percent after January 15, 10 percent after February 1 and 15 percent after March 16. Notices go out on or after October 1.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Greenville?
faqs.a: At the Greenville County Register of Deeds, 301 University Ridge, Suite S-2100, Greenville, SC 29601. The main phone is 864-467-7240, and recorders are asked to arrive before 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the buyer's tax bill change after a sale in Greenville County?
faqs.a: It can. The county says a sale can be an assessable transfer of interest, which brings a point-of-sale reassessment at current market value and removes the 15 percent cap for that transfer.

faqs.q: Why is the prior owner's name on the tax bill?
faqs.a: The county uses January 1 as its date of record. If ownership changed after that date, the prior and current owners can both be named on that year's bill, and only the current owner appears the next year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenville house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses in any condition, and the closing still runs through a South Carolina attorney and the Register of Deeds. Tell us about the property and we will talk through what we can offer.
